1	# NINEONELABS Codex Guide
2	
3	Use this file for Codex-specific repo instructions. Keep Claude-specific behavior in `CLAUDE.md`.
4	
5	## Project Defaults
6	
7	- Stack: TypeScript, SCSS, Three.js, Vite, PHP 7.4 custom MVC, MySQL, Apache via Docker
8	- Dev server: `http://localhost:8888`
9	- Default task framing: state the goal, relevant context, constraints, and done condition.
10	- For complex or ambiguous work, plan first before editing code.
11	- Prefer `chop` for long git, typecheck, and Docker inspection output when available.
12	- For read-only `git` inspection commands that may produce non-trivial output, prefer `chop` by default.
13	- Typical examples: `chop git status`, `chop git diff`, `chop git log --oneline -20`.
14	- Prefer `chop rg ...` for repository searches when the result may be longer than a few lines.
15	- For PowerShell builtins or pipeline-based inspection commands, wrap the whole script with `chop powershell -Command "..."`.
16	- Typical examples: `chop powershell -Command "Get-Content ... | Select-Object -Skip 720 -First 90"` and `chop powershell -Command "Get-Content ... | Select-String ..."`.
17	- Very short one-line commands may skip `chop`, but when in doubt prefer `chop`.
18	- **Do not run `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or `npm install`** — Vite dev server auto-rebuilds the bundle on every file save; there is no reason to run these. Only `npm install <package>` is allowed when explicitly adding a new dependency.
19	- Do not add any of these commands to agent roles, task plans, verification steps, or PR notes unless the user explicitly asks for it.
20	- On Windows PowerShell, use explicit UTF-8 for Korean text reads and writes.
21	
22	## Architecture
23	
24	- Public routes stay closure-based in `routes/web.php` and render via `render()`.
25	- Do not reintroduce Barba.js or SPA navigation contracts.
26	- Do not duplicate ownership already handled by `AppManager`, `PageRuntime`, or `PageTheatreBinder`.
27	- Keep shared engine or runtime code out of page folders.
28	- Put page scene code in `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`.
29	- Put Theatre bindings in `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`.
30	- Keep shared types in `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`.
31	
32	## Editing Rules
33	
34	- Follow existing custom MVC patterns; do not introduce Laravel or Symfony conventions.
35	- Use BEM-style naming in SCSS.
36	- Keep admin CSS and JS separate from the public SCSS pipeline.
37	- For SCSS responsive sizing, prefer shared abstract helpers such as `fluid(...)` instead of ad-hoc raw values when the project already uses that pattern.
38	- Use `#{fluid(...)}` only inside shared `abstract` or `base` files when emitting CSS custom properties or shared tokens.
39	- In component, layout, and page SCSS files, use `fluid(min, max)` directly instead of `#{fluid(...)}`.
40	- In SCSS files outside `resource/scss/abstract/` and `resource/scss/base/`, add `@use "../abstract" as *;` at the top before using shared helpers like `fluid(...)`.
41	- Do not use CSS variable fallbacks like `var(--token, fallback)` in SCSS. Use either `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly.
42	- Do not introduce base/root tokens unless the value is genuinely shared across multiple features. Avoid token waste for one-off component values.
43	- For reusable SCSS values, define the source of truth in the shared `abstract` or `base` layer first, then reference it from component or page partials.
44	- Prefer semantic tokens over raw hex values when an upstream token exists.
45	- Dispose Three.js geometries, materials, and textures.
46	- Avoid object creation inside render loops.
47	- Match event listener registration with cleanup.
48	- Never hardcode credentials or secrets.
49	
50	## Verification
51	
52	- TypeScript: `chop node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`
53	- PHP lint: `docker compose exec web php -l <file>`
54	- Diff inspection: `chop git diff`
55	- Do not use `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or `npm install` for verification; saved files are already handled by the automatic build flow.
56	- After changes, run the smallest relevant verification and report any checks not run.
57	- Review the final diff for regressions, risky patterns, and missing tests before handing off.
58	
59	## Repo Skills
60	
61	- `$scene-explorer`: inspect Three.js scene structure, Theatre bindings, and runtime ownership
62	- `$php-explorer`: inspect routes, render chains, admin structure, and backend ownership
63	
64	## Codex Notes
65	
66	- Repo-specific config lives in `.codex/config.toml`.
67	- Repo-specific execution policy lives in `.codex/rules/default.rules`.
68	- Repo hooks are intentionally omitted here because Codex hooks are currently disabled on Windows.
69	- Direct terminal commands are not auto-wrapped; use `chop <command>` explicitly when you want compressed output.
70	- Keep this file concise and durable. Add new rules only after repeated friction or repeated mistakes.
71	- Put stable repo rules here; use skills for repeatable workflows and MCP only when external, fast-changing context is required.

75	
76	To prevent Claude Code from asking for permission on every action:
77

81

83	source ~/.bashrc
84	```

86	> **Warning:** This flag auto-approves all tool use: file writes, Bash execution, etc.
87	> Use only in trusted projects. Default permission mode is recommended for unfamiliar codebases.

89	## Why npm build commands are forbidden
90	
91	`npm run build`, `npm run watch`, and `npm install` are **forbidden during normal development**.
92	
93	- **Reason:** Vite dev server at `http://localhost:8888` auto-rebuilds the bundle on every file save
94	- Running these wastes context and time with no benefit
95	- **Exception:** `npm install <package>` — only when explicitly adding a new dependency
96	- This rule is enforced in three places: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and `.claude/rules/frontend.md`
97	
98	## How the tsc PostToolUse hook works
99	
100	When a `.ts` file is modified via the Edit or Write tool, the PostToolUse hook fires automatically:
101	
102	```bash
103	# Command executed by the hook
104	chop node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
105	```
106	
107	- Hook config: `.claude/settings.json` → `PostToolUse` → matcher: `Edit|Write`
108	- If tsc errors are found, the hook returns `exit(1)`, immediately notifying Claude
109	- **How to verify:** Edit any `.ts` file with the Edit tool → check hook output for tsc results

I've completed a thorough exploration of the project structure and documentation. Here's everything you need to know:

---

### **1. ROOT-LEVEL FILES**

- **AGENTS.md** (145 lines) - Project defaults and workflow for Codex:
  - Stack details, task framing, output preferences

- **.env.example** - Configuration template (bilingual comments):

**Config/Build Files:**
- `package.json` / `package-lock.json` - Node dependencies
- `composer.json` / `composer.lock` - PHP dependencies
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript config
- `build.js` - esbuild + SCSS plugin configuration

- `makefile` - development commands (make up, make install, make migrate, etc.)

---

### **2. .CLAUDE/ DIRECTORY STRUCTURE**

**Configuration:**
- **settings.json** - Claude Code harness config:
  - allowedTools: chop, git, tsc, docker, npm test
  - PostToolUse hooks for TypeScript validation on file edits

**Documentation:**
- **BEST_PRACTICES.md** - 110-line checklist:
  - Status checks (all items ✅ complete)
  - Permission setup (--dangerously-skip-permissions in ~/.bashrc)
  - Why npm build commands are forbidden
  - How tsc PostToolUse hook works

**Rules (file-type specific guidance):**
- **rules/php.md** - Custom MVC patterns, namespace conventions, DB table naming (nb_ prefix)

- **rules/scss.md** - BEM naming, token contracts, separate admin CSS

**Agents (subagent instructions):**

- **skills/new-route/SKILL.md** - New page route + view + optional TypeScript entry

---

### **3. MAIN PAGE STRUCTURE (views/pages/index.php)**

The homepage uses a **multi-scene Three.js experience** with the following sections (data-scene attributes):

1. **intro** - Hero section with "WE DESIGN YOUR JOURNEY" title and CTA
2. **introAction** - 5-second countdown transition with Mission Control messaging
3. **hero** - Main hero with "Join The Journey" slogan
4. **story** - "Define The Design" narrative section
5. **who** - Company/team information section
6. **why** - 6 card grid (why-cards with images)
7. **services** - Services showcase
8. **portfolio-intro** - Portfolio introduction
9. **portfolio-gallery** - Portfolio gallery view
10. **clients** - Client showcase
11. **contact** - Contact/CTA section

Architecture:
- Fixed canvas layer (Three.js rendering)
- Scrollable content layer on top
- Theatre.js bindings for scene/animation management
- BEM-style CSS classes (no-main-*)

---

### **4. ROUTES & PUBLIC PAGES**

From `routes/web.php`:

**Main Routes:**
- `/` → home (pages.index)
- `/about` → pages.about.index
- `/works` → pages.works.index (with view type: scatter/grid)
- `/works/:no` → work detail view

**Architecture:**
- Closure-based routes (not controller classes)
- Data passed to views via render('pages.section', $data)
- Load works API on demand ($loadWorksApi closure)

---

### **5. PROJECT STRUCTURE SUMMARY**

```
/admin/              → Admin panel (separate CSS/JS)
/api/               → API endpoints (works.php, etc.)
/bootstrap/         → App initialization (menu.php, etc.)
/config/            → Configuration (setup.php, functions.php, helpers.php)
/database/          → Migrations
/inc/               → Shared libraries
/lang/              → Multilingual strings
/module/            → Feature modules
/resource/          → Static assets
  /css/             → Compiled CSS output
  /dist/            → Vite build output
  /images/          → Image assets
  /js/              → Legacy JS
  /scss/            → SCSS source (BEM pattern)
    /abstract/      → Shared helpers, tokens
    /base/          → Root tokens, resets
  /ts/              → TypeScript source
    /pages/         → Page-specific scene + theatre
    /manager/       → AppManager, BackgroundManager
    /runtime/       → Shared runtime code
    /objects/       → Three.js objects
    /types/         → *.types.ts (all shared types)
/routes/            → web.php (closure routes)
/src/               → Core classes (Core/, Database/, Http/, Routing/, View/, Menu/)
/views/             → Templates
  /components/      → Reusable fragments
  /layouts/         → main.php (site chrome)
  /pages/           → Page templates
  /errors/          → Error pages
```

---

### **6. KEY CONVENTIONS & RULES**

**Naming:**
- Classes: PascalCase
- Methods/variables: camelCase
- Constants: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
- DB tables: `nb_` prefix (e.g., nb_siteinfo, nb_admin)
- BEM CSS: `block__element--modifier` (e.g., no-main-hero__title)

**Tech Stack Summary:**
- **Backend:** PHP 7.4, MySQL 8.0, Custom MVC
- **Frontend:** TypeScript, Three.js, SCSS (BEM), Vite bundler
- **Build:** esbuild + esbuild-sass-plugin
- **Container:** Docker & Docker Compose
- **Testing:** Vitest (19 tests)

**Critical Prohibitions:**
- ❌ Do NOT run `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or `npm install` (Vite auto-rebuilds)
- ❌ Do NOT hardcode credentials
- ❌ Do NOT reintroduce Barba.js or SPA navigation
- ❌ Do NOT duplicate ownership (AppManager, PageRuntime, PageTheatreBinder)
- ❌ Do NOT dispose Three.js objects inside render loops

**Verification Commands:**
```bash
chop node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit          # TypeScript check
docker compose exec web php -l <file>        # PHP lint
npm run test                                  # Run tests
chop git diff                                 # Review changes
make migrate                                  # Apply migrations
```

---

### **7. EXISTING DOCUMENTATION COMPLETENESS**

✅ **Excellent coverage:**
- CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md for AI workflows
- Rules separated by file type (.ts, .scss, .php)
- Agents for backend (php-explorer) and 3D (scene-explorer)
- Skills for common tasks (migration, new-route)
- README complete with tech stack, deployment, database schema
- Best practices checklist shows all systems operational

The documentation is **well-organized, minimal, and actionable** — suitable for both human developers and AI workflows.
